en: To push too many things into a small space; or to study hard just before an exam.
ex: Students often cram for exams the night before.
學生們常在考試前一晚臨時抱佛腳。

en: Showing great happiness and health; or sending out light or heat.
ex: The bride looked radiant on her wedding day.
新娘在婚禮那天容光煥發。

en: To fight by holding and pushing an opponent; or to try hard to deal with a difficult problem.
ex: She is wrestling with a difficult decision.
她正為一個艱難的決定而苦惱。

en: Used in everyday, informal speech rather than in formal writing.
ex: "Kid" is a colloquial word for a child.
「kid」是「child」的口語說法。

en: The distance east or west of the Greenwich line, measured in degrees.
ex: The ship's position was given by its latitude and longitude.
船的位置是以經緯度標示的。

en: Toward the outside or away from the center; or what can be seen on the outside.
ex: The door opens outwards, not inwards.
這扇門向外開，不是向內開。

en: To move something quickly from side to side or up and down, as a dog does with its tail.
ex: The dog wagged its tail when its owner came home.
主人回家時，狗搖著尾巴。

en: Relating to the moon.
ex: Chinese New Year follows the lunar calendar.
農曆新年依照陰曆。

en: A person who writes plays for the theater.
ex: Shakespeare is the most famous English playwright.
莎士比亞是最有名的英國劇作家。

en: A firm demand that something should be done; or the quality of continuing to say or believe something strongly.
ex: At her insistence, they stopped to ask for directions.
在她的堅持下，他們停下來問路。

en: A person who speaks officially on behalf of a group, government or organization.
ex: A spokesperson for the company said they would investigate.
公司發言人說他們會展開調查。

en: To give a short, loud, high cry because of fear, pain or excitement; or such a cry.
ex: She shrieked when she saw the spider.
她看到蜘蛛時尖叫起來。

en: To prepare yourself for something difficult or unpleasant; or a support to hold something in place; or a device to straighten teeth.
ex: The town is bracing for a major storm.
小鎮正為一場大風暴做準備。

en: An event that interrupts the peace or normal activity; or an illness or mental problem.
ex: Police were called to a disturbance outside the bar.
警方接獲通報前往酒吧外處理騷動。

en: A freshwater fish related to the salmon, often eaten as food.
ex: He caught a large trout in the river.
他在河裡釣到一條大鱒魚。

en: A road that goes around a town or busy area; or to avoid something by going around it.
ex: The new bypass has reduced traffic in the town center.
新的繞道路減少了市中心的車流。

en: A woman who has a sexual relationship with a married man; or (old use) a woman in charge, such as a female teacher or employer.
ex: The mistress of the house welcomed the guests warmly.
女主人熱情地迎接客人。

en: A respected political leader, especially one who is wise and experienced.
ex: He was regarded as a great statesman.
他被視為一位偉大的政治家。

en: Thick, stiff paper used to make boxes and packaging.
ex: The kids made a house out of a cardboard box.
孩子們用紙箱做了一間房子。

en: To interest someone greatly; or to make secret plans; or a secret plan to do something harmful.
ex: The mystery of the old house intrigued the children.
老房子的謎團讓孩子們十分好奇。

en: A bright object with a long tail of light that moves across the night sky.
ex: Halley's comet appears about once every seventy-six years.
哈雷彗星大約每七十六年出現一次。

en: To walk or travel without a particular aim or direction.
ex: Wild horses roam freely across the plains.
野馬在平原上自由漫遊。

en: Relating to money, especially the money supply of a country.
ex: The central bank sets the country's monetary policy.
中央銀行制定該國的貨幣政策。

en: To live in a particular place (formal); or (of a power or quality) to belong to someone.
ex: The ambassador resides in a large house near the embassy.
大使住在大使館附近的一棟大房子裡。

en: A song that is officially used by a country, school or group; or a religious song.
ex: The crowd stood up and sang the national anthem.
群眾起立高唱國歌。

en: Very tired, especially after working hard for a long time; or to make or become tired.
ex: The weary travelers finally reached the inn.
疲憊的旅人終於抵達了旅店。

en: To shine with many small flashes of light; or the bright, shining quality of something.
ph: all that glitters is not gold
ex: The snow glittered in the bright morning sun.
積雪在明亮的晨光下閃閃發光。

en: To think about something for a long time in a quiet way; or to say something in a thoughtful way.
ex: "I wonder what would happen," she mused.
「不知道會發生什麼事。」她若有所思地說。

en: A small design or symbol used by a company or organization as its identity.
ex: The company changed its logo last year.
公司去年更換了標誌。

en: To pass information or a message from one person to another; or a race in which team members take turns; or a group of workers who take turns.
ex: Please relay the message to the rest of the team.
請把這個訊息轉達給團隊其他人。

en: A long piece of land that sticks out into the sea and is almost surrounded by water.
ex: Florida is a peninsula in the southeastern United States.
佛羅里達是美國東南部的一個半島。

en: A small container with medicine inside that you swallow; or the part of a spacecraft in which astronauts travel.
ex: Take one capsule with water after each meal.
每餐後用水送服一顆膠囊。

en: To send out heat, light or energy in all directions; or to spread outward from a central point.
ex: The fire radiated heat throughout the room.
爐火的熱量遍及整間房間。

en: The soft, faint light just after the sun goes down; or a period of decline.
ex: We sat on the porch and watched the twilight fade.
我們坐在門廊上，看著暮光漸漸消逝。

en: A green area with water in a desert; or a peaceful place in the middle of a busy or difficult situation.
ex: The garden was an oasis of calm in the busy city.
這座花園是繁忙城市裡的一片寧靜綠洲。

en: To gradually get more and more of something over time; or to increase in amount.
ex: Dust had accumulated on the old books.
灰塵在舊書上堆積起來。

en: To eat something quickly and hungrily; or to read or consume something with great eagerness.
ph: 狼吞虎嚥地讀完一本書
ex: The hungry children devoured the whole pizza.
飢餓的孩子們把整個披薩吃得精光。

en: A sudden, large fall in prices or sales; or to fall heavily or sit down loosely.
ex: The company's sales went into a slump last year.
公司的銷售去年陷入低迷。

en: To experience something unpleasant, such as a loss, cost or punishment, as a result of your own actions.
ex: The company incurred heavy losses last year.
公司去年蒙受了重大損失。

en: A general medical examination by a doctor to check that you are healthy.
ex: It's a good idea to have a medical checkup once a year.
每年做一次健康檢查是個好主意。
